findings.source_passage: I do deem it now a most meaning thing, that that old Greek, Prometheus, who made men, they say, should have been a blacksmith, and animated them with fire; for what's made in fire must properly belong to fire; and so hell's probable.
findings.why_it_matters: The concluding clause 'for what's made in fire must properly belong to fire; and so hell's probable' is the interpretive payload of the passage — it is Ahab's dark theology in miniature. The draft drops it entirely, leaving only the premise and none of the conclusion.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'for what's made in fire must properly belong to fire; and so hell's probable' verbatim after the Prometheus observation.

findings.source_passage: Oh, Life! Here I am, proud as Greek god, and yet standing debtor to this blockhead for a bone to stand on! Cursed be that mortal inter-indebtedness which will not do away with ledgers. I would be free as air; and I'm down in the whole world's books. I am so rich, I could have given bid for bid with the wealthiest Prætorians at the auction of the Roman empire (which was the world's); and yet I owe for the flesh in the tongue I brag with.
findings.source_locator: Ahab's soliloquy after dismissing the carpenter
findings.why_it_matters: The Prætorian auction sentence and 'I owe for the flesh in the tongue I brag with' are among the most rhetorically distinctive lines in the chapter — they establish Ahab's cosmic self-conception and bitter irony about embodied dependence. Both are absent from the draft.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Prætorian / Roman Empire sentence and 'I owe for the flesh in the tongue I brag with' verbatim before the crucible line.

findings.source_passage: he's queer; says nothing but that one sufficient little word queer; he's queer, says Stubb; he's queer—queer, queer; and keeps dinning it into Mr. Starbuck all the time—queer—sir—queer, queer, very queer.
findings.why_it_matters: The incantatory, repetitive rhythm of 'queer' is itself the comic voice of the carpenter — the draft reduces it to 'Stubb ever says he's queer—queer, queer,' losing the full hypnotic accumulation that is the passage's rhetorical signature.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the extended queer-repetition chain more fully, including the detail about 'dinning it into Mr. Starbuck.'

findings.source_passage: a short, little old body like me, should never undertake to wade out into deep waters with tall, heron-built captains; the water chucks you under the chin pretty quick, and there's a great cry for life-boats.
findings.why_it_matters: This comic self-deprecating simile is the carpenter's most distinctive voice moment — it establishes his character as a humble, sensible counterpoint to Ahab's grandeur and is a key piece of register-defining prose.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'heron-built captains' / water-chucks-you-under-the-chin passage in the carpenter's closing monologue.

findings.source_passage: I am so rich, I could have given bid for bid with the wealthiest Prætorians at the auction of the Roman empire (which was the world's)
findings.why_it_matters: This parenthetical aside—'(which was the world's)'—is a signature Melvillean compression carrying enormous interpretive weight about Ahab's sense of scale and the novel's imperial thematics; its omission flattens the speech.
findings.suggested_fix: Include the Prætorian sentence with its parenthetical in Ahab's soliloquy.

findings.source_passage: What's Prometheus about there?—the blacksmith, I mean—what's he about? He makes a fierce red flame there!
findings.why_it_matters: The double-question and exclamation give Ahab's attention to the forge a kinetic, restless quality; the draft compresses this to a single smooth sentence losing the characteristic dash-driven rhythm.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain the double question and the 'fierce red flame' exclamation in their original syntactic shape.

summary: Two high-severity losses (the 'hell's probable' conclusion of the Prometheus passage, and the Prætorian/Roman Empire/tongue sentence of Ahab's soliloquy) plus multiple medium-severity voice erasures in both the carpenter's comic monologue and Ahab's rhetoric require regeneration.
